**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**No exit codes are listed per command.** The register's per-command exit tables are measurements of _v2_, and v3 does not reproduce them everywhere, so they are not published here as v3's contract. Every command follows the one surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes).

## `intent estate`

Every Claude session on this host: who it is, where it stands, and what it is doing

```
intent estate <command>
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.6`     | **no -- newer than the release**                           |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values | Notes |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `command` | `subcommand` | yes      |        |       |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent estate --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent estate status`

```

```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.6`     | **no -- newer than the release**                           |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | yes                                                        |

**Flags**

| Flag        | Takes              | Default    | What it does                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--format`  | `<terminal\|json>` | `terminal` | Output format                                                          |
| `--browser` | no                 |            | Open the estate page in the browser, served by intentd                 |

## `intent estate control`

Take, release or hold control of this host's slots: the controller alone grants, and holds stop every grant

```
intent estate control <verb> [<arg>] [flags]
```

|                 |                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.6`     | **no -- newer than the release** |
| Reads or writes | mutate                           |
| Undo            | one-way                          |
| Over MCP        | no                               |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type         | Required | Values                              | Notes                                                 |
| -------- | ------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `verb`   | `subcommand` | yes      | `take`, `release`, `hold`, `unhold` |                                                       |
| `arg`    | `string`     | no       |                                     | The condition for `hold`, the hold's id for `unhold`. |

**Flags**

| Flag     | Takes     | Default | What it does                                                                       |
| -------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--hv`   | `<words>` |         | hv's words, verbatim, for a take under a name other than the recorded controller's |
| `--node` | `<node>`  |         | The whiteboard node this session is, recorded on the write                         |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent estate control --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent estate lane`

Open, close or hold a lane: a scarce resource with a running capacity that grants are checked against

```
intent estate lane <verb> <lane> [<arg>] [flags]
```

|                 |                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.6`     | **no -- newer than the release** |
| Reads or writes | mutate                           |
| Undo            | one-way                          |
| Over MCP        | no                               |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type         | Required | Values                            | Notes                                                 |
| -------- | ------------ | -------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `verb`   | `subcommand` | yes      | `open`, `close`, `hold`, `unhold` |                                                       |
| `lane`   | `string`     | yes      |                                   |                                                       |
| `arg`    | `string`     | no       |                                   | The condition for `hold`, the hold's id for `unhold`. |

**Flags**

| Flag           | Takes    | Default | What it does                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--type`       | `<type>` |         | The lane's type, the class the controller names (eg heavy, light, negligible) |
| `--capacity`   | `<n>`    |         | How many requests may be granted or running in the lane at once               |
| `--load-under` | `<load>` |         | Admit a grant into the lane only while the 1-minute load is under this        |
| `--node`       | `<node>` |         | The whiteboard node this session is, recorded on the write                    |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent estate lane --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## `intent estate slots`

Ask for a slot, wait for the answer and run in it, or, as the controller, grant, deny or revoke one and watch them all

```
intent estate slots <verb> [<subject>] [<text>] [flags]
```

|                 |                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- |
| In `v3.2.6`     | **no -- newer than the release** |
| Reads or writes | mutate                           |
| Undo            | one-way                          |
| Over MCP        | no                               |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values                                                                           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verb`    | `subcommand` | yes      | `ask`, `grant`, `deny`, `revoke`, `start`, `release`, `wait`, `watch`, `pending` |                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `subject` | `string`     | no       |                                                                                  | The request type for `ask`; the request id for `grant`, `deny`, `revoke`, `start`, `release` and `wait`, each of which refuses without it; `watch` and `pending` take none. |
| `text`    | `string`     | no       |                                                                                  | What the run is, for `ask`; the reason, for `deny` and `revoke`.                                                                                                            |

**Flags**

| Flag           | Takes         | Default | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--lane`       | `<lane,...>`  |         | For ask, the lane preferred; for grant, every lane the run holds, comma-separated, or `none`                                                                                                        |
| `--named`      | `<k=v,...>`   |         | What the booking runs, as key=value pairs, comma-separated (eg tip=,patch_id=)                                                                                                                      |
| `--tag`        | `<tag,...>`   |         | Tags shown on the request, comma-separated; they order nothing                                                                                                                                      |
| `--not-before` | `<id,...>`    |         | Request ids that must end before this one is granted, comma-separated                                                                                                                               |
| `--hold`       | `<condition>` |         | A condition the controller judges before granting, shown on the request                                                                                                                             |
| `--place-of`   | `<id>`        |         | A hand-back keeping its place: the request this one re-asks for                                                                                                                                     |
| `--result`     | `<text>`      |         | The run's result as the holder writes it, recorded on release                                                                                                                                       |
| `--relayed`    | no            |         | The stamp is a relay's time, for a run on another host, not the run's own clock                                                                                                                     |
| `--timeout`    | `<seconds>`   |         | For wait, the seconds to wait for the controller's answer, with none waiting as long as the ask stands; wait exits 0 granted, 1 denied or revoked, and 4 with the ask still standing at the timeout |
| `--node`       | `<node>`      |         | The whiteboard node this session is, recorded on the write                                                                                                                                          |

**Exit codes** follow the surface-wide contract on the [index](index.md#exit-codes) (INV-04). `intent estate slots --help`, and your own binary, are the authority on this verb.

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
